validity.recommendation: Reclassify PipelineType from 'transmission' to a gathering/feeder line: this is the 14-in raw-gas feeder from Nasiriyah field into the Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas-processing/flare-recovery plant, not a transmission trunk.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed and real. The sheet's sole cited source (al-mirbad.com/detail/157543, dated 2 May 2024, a program interview with the project supervisory committee of South Gas Company / شركة غاز الجنوب) is live and directly on-point. It states the raw feed gas ('الغاز المغذي الخام') to the Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas investment project arrives via two pipes: pipe #1 = 20-inch, 120 MMcf/d from Gharraf field; pipe #2 = 14-inch, 80 MMcf/d from the Nasiriyah field ('الأنبوب الثاني من 14 ... بطاقة 80 مقمق من حقل الناصرية'). P7445 is that second (Nasiriyah) feeder. Existence is independently corroborated: Egypt Oil & Gas ('Iraq's Nasiriyah, Gharraf Gas Fields Project Nears Operational Phase') and Baker Hughes ('SGC awards BHGE contract for recovery of flare gas for Nassiriya and Al Gharraf oilfields') both confirm the same project (~200 MMcf/d combined processing, South Gas Company operator, Baker Hughes/CPECC as contractors, Q1-2027 startup). Not GEM-only. CLASSIFICATION (the concern): al-mirbad explicitly describes P7445 as a raw-feed-gas intake pipe delivering wet associated gas from the wellfield to a processing plant that then produces dry gas / LPG via 'field processing and plant processing' ('معالجة حقلية ومعالجة مصنعية'). That is a gathering/feeder line, not a transmission pipeline; GEM's PipelineType='transmission' is misclassified. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any roster PID -- the companion 20-in/120-MMcf/d Gharraf feeder from the same project is NOT in the roster, so P7445 is the sole GEM entry for the Nasiriyah leg. ATTRIBUTION confirmed: operator South Gas Company and owner Iraq Ministry of Oil (SGC is the Ministry's southern gas arm) match al-mirbad + Baker Hughes; FuelSource 'Nasiriyah Field' and StartState/Province 'Dhi Qar' (Nasiriyah is the Dhi Qar capital) both correct. SPEC: diameter 14-in and capacity 80 MMcf/d match al-mirbad exactly (single strong primary source -> medium confidence); minor caveat -- aggregate coverage (S&P/Egypt Oil & Gas) frames Nasiriyah's flared-gas volume as ~70 MMcf/d vs the 80 MMcf/d pipe capacity, a small, non-material difference (flared-volume vs pipe rating).

fills.researcher_notes: al-mirbad (2 May 2024) documents construction actively underway in 2024 -- equipment installation, mechanical works, tie-in of the field pipes and in-site pipe networks -- supporting the recorded ConstructionYear=2024. Caveat: aggregate sources (S&P Global) date the overall MoU project's construction start to 2022; the 2024 value is defensible for the on-site build phase but the year is somewhat soft. Single source -> medium.

Operator was MISSING_REF. al-mirbad names South Gas Company (شركة غاز الجنوب) as the entity overseeing the Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas project; Baker Hughes' contract-award release confirms 'SGC' (South Gas Company) as the awarding operator for flare-gas recovery at Nassiriya and Al-Gharraf. Two independent sources -> high.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'construction' still correct. al-mirbad (May 2024) had the feeder pipes being tied in and equipment installed. The newest evidence -- Egypt Oil & Gas 'Nears Operational Phase' (contemporaneous with Iraq Business News' Dec 2025 'to begin ops in 2027' piece, which returned 401 so is not cited) -- reports equipment fully delivered, on-site installation underway, and first operations expected Q1 2027. Not yet operating, no shelving/cancellation signal; construction is active and progressing. Not stale (well within dormancy thresholds; active build). No date-column change needed.

summary: P7445 Nasiriyah Field Gas Pipeline: real and under construction (Q1-2027 startup) but MISCLASSIFIED -- it is the 14-in/80-MMcf/d raw-gas feeder from Nasiriyah field into the Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas-processing plant, not a transmission trunk; reclassify to gathering. Filled missing Operator + Construction refs; status 'construction' confirmed.
